Global Instances of Coups, 1950 – Present

Note (8.29.2026): Data have been tentatively updated to reflect a coup attempt in Niger on August 29, 2026. The coding will be updated to reflect the outcome within one week. There will be larger updates to the data in the coming weeks that will lead to substantial revisions. Previous versions of the data will be archived below.

This project is a collaborative effort with Clayton Thyne to document successful and failed coups throughout the world. The initial data project, published in Journal of Peace Research, covered 1950-2009. We have continued to provide regular updates to the data.

We define coups as “illegal and overt attempts by the military or other elites within the state apparatus to unseat the sitting executive.” Successes are treated as episodes in which the perpetrators (or their agents) control power for at least 7 days. All data on this page are updated regularly. I strongly encourage anyone with comments, questions, or concerns with the data to contact Jonathan Powell or Clayton Thyne.
